newsitem.title: USA: Metropolitan Health to acquire Trident.
newsitem.headline: Metropolitan Health to acquire Trident.

text.p: Metropolitan Health Networks Inc, a medical group practice, said on Thursday it had executed a letter of intent to acquire all of the outstanding shares of Trident Medical Concepts Inc in a stock deal.
The company said in a statement it will issue one share for each Trident share as part of the terms of the deal.
Trident, a medical management company, has about 4.9 million shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis, it added.
On Thursday, Metropolitan's stock was trading up 1 at 5 on the Nasdaq.
The company said it expected the combined companies to have a minimum of $32 million in current revenues at the time of the deal's closing.
It also said Anthony Gigliotti, chairman and chief executive officer of Trident, will become chairman and chief executive officer of Metropolitan.
Noel Guillama is to step down as chief executive at Metropolitan to become its president, it said.
A spokesman for the company said Metropolitan will move its national headquarters from Boca Raton, Florida to a new facility in West Palm Beach in the same state, where Trident is located.
A spokesman for the company said he was "unaware" of any plans to lay off staff.
Metropolitan said in its statement that the deal also obliged Trident to have a minimum of $20 million in current (run-rate) revenues at the time of closing.

Trident, which has operations in Florida, Georgia, Maryland, Virginia and California, has executed letters of intent to acquire about $100 million in revenues from seven facilities in Maryland, Florida, and New York, it said.
It has plans to raise up to $50 million in the form of debt or equity in order to finance its acquisition strategy and operations, it added.
